objective: Close the privilege-policy debt left open by the rename: remove every code path that invokes a privilege-bypass tool, make pkexec the only default elevation mechanism, and remove the dead sudo-named CLI surface.
scope: findElevator defaults to pkexec and rejects CALIX_ELEVATOR=sudo, doas or su with error.ForbiddenElevator
pkexec invoking-user drops use pkexec's native --user option instead of sudo/doas's -u convention
SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH AUR builds drop to the invoking user through runuser instead of sudo
database-lock remediation now prints pkexec rm and all affected expectations were updated
the no-op calix utility --sudo/-s flag was removed from the catalog and option handling
isolated-build and cancellation harnesses use pkexec/runuser and skip with exit 77 without a polkit session
operational documentation and manual-test instructions now describe polkit/pkexec
SUDO_USER and DOAS_USER remain detection-only markers for externally launched processes; Calix never invokes those tools

policy.invoking_user_drop: pkexec --user USER /usr/bin/env -i ...; test harness drops use runuser

isolated_harnesses.reason: no interactive polkit authentication agent is available to the unattended harness

known_gaps: Real pkexec plus systemd-nspawn execution was not run unattended: both harnesses correctly exit 77 rather than prompting without a polkit agent.
The --sudo/-s utility flag was removed rather than aliased; scripts that used the no-op flag now receive an unknown-option error.
calix-daemon packaging and the user service remain the next approved phase.
GitHub Actions was not triggered for this commit; the container replay is the pre-push proof.

real isolated build and cancellation flows through systemd-nspawn
pacman package installation on the host
